_about: The deep active vision models of the timeline slide, each read in its paper (evidence, quotes and figure pages in literature.md, section Prior active vision). date: first public release (arXiv v1). name: the model's name. cite: authors, venue and venue year. policy: how it chooses where to look: 'rl' when the choice is learned by reinforcement learning (named in method), else what it uses. row: where the label sits, -3, -2 and -1 above the axis, 1 and 2 below, chosen so that labels do not overlap. Selection [Yohaï, 2026-10-01]: each entry precise and distinctive; STAM (CVPR 2022) was dropped: the CanViT paper does not cite it and never seeing the whole image is not what sets it apart (RAM's glimpses do not cover it either). canvit: CanViT itself, drawn on the slide's last click as the axis extends into 2026; date: arXiv v1 of arXiv:2603.22570, submitted 23 March 2026 (read on its arXiv page, 2026-10-01). neuro_ai: active-vision models built to compare with brain or behavioral data, drawn on their own click [2026-10-23]; read on their abstract pages (2026-10-23): GVSM, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.06.658387, posted 2025-06-10: visual search from pixels in natural scenes, compared with human scanpaths and primate fronto-parietal activity; GPN, arXiv:2511.12715 v1 2025-11-16: predicts the next glimpse's embedding along human-like scanpaths, compared with human fMRI. How each obtains its viewpoints is not stated in the abstracts and is not claimed here. neuro_ai entries are drawn like the models, name and citation on a leader, at their row. pioneer: true for the model the field traces back to (the paper's Related work: "This line of research traces back to the Recurrent Attention Model"), highlighted on the slide.
